\hypertarget{what-the-folder-contains-and-why}{%
\section{1. What the folder contains, and
why}\label{what-the-folder-contains-and-why}}

The folder \texttt{vendor/sundials\_rs-7.8.0} of PROJECT spacetimes
contains a translation into the programming language Rust of SUNDIALS
7.8.0 (SUite of Nonlinear and DIfferential/ALgebraic equation Solvers,
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory): every function of the C
library, with the same names, constants and return flags, written in
safe Rust (no \texttt{unsafe} block, no foreign library, no crate from
crates.io). It is a copy, without any change, of the folder
\texttt{sundials\_rs} of the repository of the author of PROJECT
spacetimes,

\begin{verbatim}
https://github.com/once-ere/rustSolveIt_macos-silicon_SUNDIALS_7_8_0
\end{verbatim}

at the commit \texttt{f656982a9eed262f5d99a7dba1753f3f19171f87}
(2026-10-31 06:41:05 -0700, message ``Create LICENSE'').

\textbf{Why.} On 2026-11-18 the author instructed that the time
integrations of the project must not use a hand-written fixed-step
method (the classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta method, RK4, of the
programs of Test 2) and must use instead the pure-Rust CVODE of this
repository, or another applicable SUNDIALS algorithm. The programs of
\texttt{Revision\_SuperLoop/test2/rust} therefore integrate every
time-dependent equation with CVODE from this folder. CVODE is part of
the crate \texttt{cvode\_rs}; it needs the crate
\texttt{sundials\_core}. The other five crates are copied as well, so
that the folder is the complete translation and later work (for example
the redo of older calculations) can use IDA, KINSOL, CVODES or ARKODE
without a second copy.

\hypertarget{the-files-that-were-copied}{%
\section{2. The files that were
copied}\label{the-files-that-were-copied}}

From the folder \texttt{sundials\_rs} of the source repository the
following were copied byte for byte (283 files in all):

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{Cargo.toml} (the workspace of the seven crates, version
  7.8.0), \texttt{Cargo.lock}, \texttt{LICENSE}, \texttt{NOTICE},
  \texttt{.gitattributes};
\item
  the folder \texttt{crates} with the seven crates of the table below.
\end{itemize}

Not copied (none of them is needed to build or to use the crates): the
\texttt{README.md} of the translation and its other documentation files,
and the folders \texttt{c-results}, \texttt{rust-results},
\texttt{differences}, \texttt{evidence}, \texttt{examples} (the tree of
the upstream C examples with their reference outputs \texttt{.out}),
\texttt{logs} and \texttt{tools} (the verification of the translation
against the C library).

\hypertarget{the-licences}{%
\section{3. The licences}\label{the-licences}}

\texttt{LICENSE} is the BSD 3-Clause licence of SUNDIALS (Lawrence
Livermore National Security, Southern Methodist University, University
of Maryland Baltimore County and the SUNDIALS contributors), copied
verbatim from the upstream tree by the translation. \texttt{NOTICE}
states the two licences that apply: the BSD 3-Clause licence of SUNDIALS
for everything under \texttt{crates/}, and the MIT licence (Copyright
(c) 2018, Arm Limited) of the pure-Rust \texttt{pow} function in
\texttt{crates/sundials\_core/src/sundials\_math.rs}, which comes from
the ARM optimized-routines through musl. Both licences permit copying
with these notices, which travel with the folder.

\hypertarget{how-project-spacetimes-uses-the-folder}{%
\section{4. How PROJECT spacetimes uses the
folder}\label{how-project-spacetimes-uses-the-folder}}

The library \texttt{t2core} of Test 2 declares in
\texttt{Revision\_SuperLoop/test2/rust/t2core/Cargo.toml}

\begin{verbatim}
cvode_rs = { path = "../../../../vendor/sundials_rs-7.8.0/crates/cvode_rs" }
\end{verbatim}

(a path dependency: Cargo builds the crate from this folder; nothing is
downloaded). The module \texttt{t2core::cvode} (file
\texttt{Revision\_SuperLoop/test2/rust/t2core/src/cvode.rs}) calls these
functions of SUNDIALS: \texttt{SUNContext\_Create},
\texttt{N\_VNew\_Serial}, \texttt{NV\_DATA\_S}, \texttt{CVodeCreate}
(with \texttt{CV\_ADAMS} or \texttt{CV\_BDF}), \texttt{CVodeInit},
\texttt{CVodeWFtolerances}, \texttt{CVodeSetMaxOrd},
\texttt{CVodeSetMaxNumSteps}, \texttt{CVodeSetUserData},
\texttt{SUNNonlinSol\_FixedPoint}, \texttt{CVodeSetNonlinearSolver},
\texttt{CVode} (with \texttt{CV\_NORMAL}), \texttt{CVodeGetNumSteps},
\texttt{CVodeGetNumRhsEvals}, \texttt{CVodeGetNumErrTestFails},
\texttt{CVodeGetNumNonlinSolvIters},
\texttt{CVodeGetNumNonlinSolvConvFails}, \texttt{CVodeGetLastOrder},
\texttt{CVodeGetLastStep}, \texttt{CVodeFree},
\texttt{SUNNonlinSolFree}, \texttt{N\_VDestroy} and
\texttt{SUNContext\_Free}.

\textbf{The method, in brief} (so that this document can be read alone;
the symbols are those of the registry of the folder Revision\_SuperLoop,
where they are defined: \(x^0_{\rm LL}\) the time,
\(w^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}\) a Nambu mode on the lattice as one complex
vector, \(w^{\rm cmp}_{\rm LL}\) one of its complex components,
\(n^{\rm cpx}_{\rm LL}\) their number, \(\mathcal H^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}\)
the lattice operator, \(h^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) and
\(q^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) the size and the order of an internal step of
CVODE, \(r^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}\) and \(a^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}\) its
relative and absolute tolerance). CVODE integrates real systems of
differential equations of the first order in the time. The programs of
Test 2 store the complex vector \(w^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}\) as the real
vector of the real and imaginary parts of its components and give CVODE
the right side \(-i\mathcal H^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}w^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}\)
of
\(i\,\partial_0w^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}=\mathcal H^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}w^{\rm lat}_{\rm LL}\)
in the same form. CVODE advances the solution with linear multistep
formulas: a step of the size \(h^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) computes the new
state from the right side at the new time and from the states and right
sides at earlier step times, with coefficients that follow from the
order \(q^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) and from the recent step sizes. The
Adams-Moulton formulas (for nonstiff problems, orders 1 to 12) use the
new right side and the right sides at the \(q^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}-1\)
preceding step times; the backward differentiation formulas (BDF, stiff
problems, orders 1 to 5) use the new right side and the states at the
\(q^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) preceding step times. The formula is implicit in
the new state; with the fixed-point (functional) iteration of
\texttt{SUNNonlinSol\_FixedPoint} the new state is found by repeated
evaluation of the right side. Every step is accepted only if the
estimated local error passes the test
\[\Big(\frac{1}{2n^{\rm cpx}_{\rm LL}}\sum_{w^{\rm cmp}_{\rm LL}}\frac{\lvert\text{estimated local error of }w^{\rm cmp}_{\rm LL}\rvert^2}{\big(r^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}\lvert w^{\rm cmp}_{\rm LL}\rvert+a^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}\big)^2}\Big)^{1/2}\le1\]
(the weighted root-mean-square norm of SUNDIALS over the
\(2n^{\rm cpx}_{\rm LL}\) real components, with the weight
\(1/(r^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}\lvert w^{\rm cmp}_{\rm LL}\rvert+a^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL})\)
for the real and for the imaginary part of every complex component,
which the programs of Test 2 give to CVODE through their own
error-weight function, \texttt{CVodeWFtolerances}); otherwise the step
is repeated with a smaller \(h^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\). CVODE changes
\(h^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) and \(q^{\rm CV}_{\rm LL}\) so that the steps
are as large as this test allows, and returns the state at requested
output times \(x^0_{\rm LL}\) from its interpolating polynomial.

\hypertarget{the-verification-that-was-performed}{%
\section{5. The verification that was
performed}\label{the-verification-that-was-performed}}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Identity of the copy.} The 283 SHA-256 digests of the copied
  files equal those of the source files (Appendix A).
\item
  \textbf{No unsafe code.} The word \texttt{unsafe} occurs in 7 lines of
  the 280 Rust files, and in each of them only inside a documentation
  comment stating that the crate contains no \texttt{unsafe} code.
\item
  \textbf{Build.} On Linux x86-64 with rustc 1.97.0 and cargo 1.97.0,
  \texttt{cargo\ build\ -\/-release\ -p\ cvode\_rs} in
  \texttt{vendor/sundials\_rs-7.8.0} compiled \texttt{sundials\_core}
  and \texttt{cvode\_rs} in 16.3 s without a warning.
\item
  \textbf{Examples against the upstream reference outputs.} The Rust
  examples were run and their printed output was compared with the
  reference outputs \texttt{.out} of the upstream C examples (from the
  folder \texttt{examples} of the source repository, which was not
  copied):
\end{enumerate}

\texttt{cvRoberts\_dns} & BDF with the dense linear solver and root

The SHA-256 digest of the output of \texttt{cvDirectDemo\_ls}, and of
its reference output, is
\texttt{a19abd5087bb90d0831b1b2d329c546590de99a12fa6bd2573a172cf31e950a7}.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The use in Test 2.} The unit test of \texttt{t2core::cvode}
  integrates one complex component that oscillates with a fixed energy
  (the energy 1.7, over 100 periods, with
  \(r^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}=10^{-12}\) and
  \(a^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}=10^{-14}\)) and compares it with the exact
  oscillation (deviation below \(10^{-8}\)); the check GS-13 of the
  program \texttt{t2\_fields} compares CVODE on a lattice with random
  gauge and pair fields with the exact spectral solution (relative
  deviation \(1.7\times10^{-10}\) at \(r^{\rm tol}_{\rm LL}=10^{-12}\)).
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Running the examples writes files.} Some examples write their
own output files into the current folder (for example
\texttt{cvRoberts\_dns} writes \texttt{cvRoberts\_dns\_stats.csv},
\texttt{cvPendulum\_dns} writes eleven \texttt{cvPendulum\_dns\_*.txt}).
Run them from a scratch folder, or remove these files afterwards; they
are not part of the vendored copy.

verification}\label{how-to-repeat-the-verification}}

\ExtensionTok{cargo}\NormalTok{ build }\AttributeTok{{-}{-}release} \AttributeTok{{-}p}\NormalTok{ cvode\_rs}
\FunctionTok{mkdir} \AttributeTok{{-}p}\NormalTok{ /tmp/cvode\_examples }\KeywordTok{\&\&} \BuiltInTok{cd}\NormalTok{ /tmp/cvode\_examples}
\ExtensionTok{cargo}\NormalTok{ run }\AttributeTok{{-}{-}release} \AttributeTok{{-}{-}manifest{-}path} \StringTok{"/Users/nsh/Developer/github/spacetimes/vendor/sundials\_rs{-}7.8.0/Cargo.toml"} \AttributeTok{{-}p}\NormalTok{ cvode\_rs }\AttributeTok{{-}{-}example}\NormalTok{ cvDirectDemo\_ls}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The first command checks every digest (on Linux:
\texttt{sha256sum\ -c\ SHA256SUMS.txt}); the second builds CVODE; the
last two run the demonstration program in a scratch folder.
